threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the train'—everyone here knows it's more than just a subway.
Last night on the 133, a guy quietly settled into a seat, then pulled out a full-on chess set. He set it up right there. The driver didn’t bat an eye.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the kebab shop owner doing a spontaneous dance to a street musician's tune while the pigeons gathered around was when I knew I belonged.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how remnants of Berlin Wall graffiti still pop up on random buildings? It's like the city's secrets are hiding in plain sight.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they’ve learned to dodge that guy selling fruit at 16th and Mission like it’s a sport. Tourists just stop and stare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Riding the 14 Mission, I saw a guy in a tuxedo lose his shoe while sprinting after the bus. Classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists miss that the best plaça in Gràcia isn’t the busy ones like Virreina, but the quiet nooks like la plaça del Sol after sunset, when locals gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily—still clutching their maps, eyes wide at menus, and asking for 'tapas' in English. It’s adorable, really.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for 'the best coffee' and locals just stare, because it depends on the day, mood, and who’s behind the counter.
Last night on the 59, a bloke argued with a kebab shop owner about which sauce is better. Laughter echoed louder than the engine.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a street musician playing classical violin next to a guy selling döner at 2 AM. That mix of cultures hits different.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you see a spontaneous street party break out after a BVG strike announcement. It's like a dance-off with public transport as the backdrop.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local knows to sidestep the dog on the tracks near Civic Center, while visitors stand there confused. That's a true San Francisco hazard.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 at 8 AM today, only to find it paused because a guy was trying to negotiate with a raccoon on the tracks. Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think it’s all about the parks, but the real vibe is in the hidden alleys where the locals gather for vermut after work.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they still look down at their phones, completely missing the street art that brightens the corners.
